Space is a vacuum and sound waves can’t travel through it in the same way they do on Earth, meaning you wouldn't be able to hear anything in space. But space isn’t entirely silent. Electromagnetic vibrations, like plasma waves or magnetic field interactions, can be translated into sound by instruments. ## What would happen if a tablespoonful of a neutron star was brought to Earth?
A tablespoon of the Sun, depending on where you scoop, would weigh about 5 pounds (2 kilograms) — the weight of an old laptop. A tablespoon of neutron star weighs more than 1 billion tons (900 billion kg) — the weight of Mount Everest. So while you could lift a spoonful of Sun, you can’t lift a spoonful of neutron star.

plan.title: 5 Weird Facts About Space
plan.description: Five strange space facts: silent space that can be sonified, a floating planet, a very long Mercury day, a heavy teaspoon of neutron star, and space sickness. A quick tour of how odd the universe really is.

beats.narration: One planet in our solar system is lighter than water. Saturn is less dense than water, so it could float in a bathtub, if anybody could build a bathtub big enough.
On Mercury, a day is longer than a year. One year lasts 88 Earth days. But sunrise to sunrise takes 176 Earth days, twice as long.

props.label: Sunrise to sunrise on Mercury, twice its 88-day year

beats.narration: A teaspoon of neutron star would weigh over a billion tons on Earth. You can lift a spoonful of the Sun, about five pounds. Not this.
Space is silent, because sound can't travel through a vacuum. But NASA turns data from planets, stars and black holes into eerie sounds we can hear.
And space can make you sick. Over half of astronauts get nausea, headaches or vomiting. So the universe is weird, even for those who go there.

props.text: Over half of astronauts get space sickness.
